lessons.title: [ ]: square brackets
lessons.tip: Square brackets are to the right of P, at the very end of the top row: your right little finger reaches up to them, without Shift.

tuto.intro: Square brackets [ ] are typed with your right little finger, on the two keys to the right of P. They are used in code (list[0]) and for added words in square brackets. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Your right little finger stretches past P: [ is just to the right, ] just after it. No Shift is needed.
Every bracket you open must be closed. Chain it together: open, type, close.
list[0], data[3], item[i]: the square bracket picks out a slot in a list.

tuto.tip: Goal: type [ and ] with your right little finger without leaving your home position.

lessons.title: { }: curly braces
lessons.tip: Curly braces are on the same keys as square brackets, with Shift: your right little finger reaches up, and your left little finger holds Shift.

tuto.intro: Curly braces { } share the keys of the square brackets: you get them with Shift. You meet them in code and stylesheets. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Just like capital letters: hold Shift with the little finger of the hand that is not typing the key. Shift plus the number key gives the symbol.
Like square brackets: a brace you open must be closed. Get into the habit of typing them in pairs.
{style: bold}, {x: 1}: braces mark out a block of code or an object.

tuto.tip: Goal: type { and } with Shift and your right little finger.

lessons.title: \ and |: backslash and vertical bar
lessons.tip: The backslash and the vertical bar are on the key just above Enter, typed with your right little finger; the vertical bar needs Shift.

tuto.intro: The backslash \ and the vertical bar | share one key, right at the end of the top row, above Enter. You get the vertical bar with Shift. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Your right little finger stretches to the end of the top row, past the square brackets. \ is typed on its own, | with Shift.
C:\Users\Tom: the backslash separates folders in Windows, whereas the plain forward slash / separates them elsewhere.
a | b joins two commands or separates two choices: left | right.

tuto.tip: Goal: type \ and | with your right little finger, with Shift for the vertical bar.

lessons.text: C:\Users\Tom a|b a||b c\d \n \t left | right /home | grep \\ || C:\Windows

lessons.title: < >: angle brackets
lessons.tip: Angle brackets are on the comma and full stop keys, with Shift: your right middle and ring fingers reach down, and your left little finger holds Shift.

tuto.intro:
Angle brackets < > are typed with Shift on the comma and full stop keys. You see them in HTML tags:

text

. The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Just like capital letters: hold Shift with the little finger of the hand that is not typing the key. Shift plus the number key gives the symbol.

text

: the opening bracket, the name of the tag, the closing bracket. The forward slash / closes the tag.
Every tag you open is closed with the forward slash. Practise chaining the two.

tuto.tip: Goal: type < and > with Shift and the fingers of your right hand.

lessons.title: Review: all the symbols in text
lessons.tip: We bring all the symbols together in a text mixing an address, the web, code and prices. Spot the movement before each symbol: direct, Shift or dead key.

tuto.intro: We bring all the symbols together in a text mixing an email address, the web, code and percentages. The big mix! The exact movement for your keyboard is shown just below.

rules.d: Shift, dead keys, direct signs: each symbol has its own movement. Use everything you learned in the last two modules.
Before each symbol, identify it: direct, Shift or dead key? This reflex saves you time.
Mastering the symbols means typing an address, a piece of code or a formula without ever getting stuck.

tuto.tip: Goal: chain all the symbols together in real text, each movement at the right moment.
